content_sections.heading: ACTREC Junior Research Fellow Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: M.Sc. or equivalent in Life Sciences/Basic Sciences, or M.Tech in Biotechnology, from a recognised university with at least 60% aggregate marks. Candidates must also have qualified CSIR-UGC NET, GATE or any other national-level entrance for pursuing PhD. A one-year M.Sc. degree will not be considered. Preference goes to candidates with experience in molecular biology, mice handling and mammalian cell culture. This experience is preferred, not mandatory. For the full eligibility conditions, see the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The appointment is for six months at first and can be extended. ACTREC will monitor each candidate's work progress, and an extension may be given after 6 months. The JRF may be upgraded to SRF in future, depending on qualifications and the required experience.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is through a walk-in interview. The notice does not mention a written test.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for ACTREC Junior Research Fellow Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Check that you meet the essential qualification, including NET, GATE or another qualifying national-level entrance. Bring the documents listed below. Report between 10:00 am and 10:30 am on Thursday, 12 November 2026, at Meeting Room I, 3rd Floor, Khanolkar Shodhika, ACTREC, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai - 410210. Take part in the interview. Recent CV Original certificates and testimonials, plus photocopies Recent passport-size photograph ID proof (preferably Aadhaar Card)

faq.question: Q1. Where is the ACTREC JRF walk-in interview held?
faq.answer: The interview is at Meeting Room I, 3rd Floor, Khanolkar Shodhika, ACTREC, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai - 410210.

faq.question: Q2. What time should I report?
faq.answer: Reporting time is 10:00 am to 10:30 am on the interview day.

faq.question: Q3. How is the Rs. 46,990 salary made up?
faq.answer: It is Rs. 37,000 plus 27% HRA, paid as a consolidated monthly amount.

faq.question: Q4. Is a NET or GATE qualification compulsory?
faq.answer: Yes. You must have qualified CSIR-UGC NET, GATE or any other national-level entrance for pursuing PhD, in addition to the 60% aggregate in your postgraduate degree.

faq.question: Q5. Can I apply with a one-year M.Sc. degree?
faq.answer: No. The notice states that a one-year M.Sc. degree will not be considered.

faq.question: Q6. Which experience gives an advantage?
faq.answer: Experience in molecular biology, mice handling and mammalian cell culture is preferred.

faq.question: Q7. What will the fellow work on?
faq.answer: The fellow will work on the project "Delineating the molecular signalling mechanism that impacts chemo-resistance in human oral cancer stem cells".

faq.question: Q8. Can the JRF become an SRF later?
faq.answer: Yes, the JRF may be upgraded to SRF in future, based on qualifications and the required experience.

faq.question: Q9. Which ID proof should I bring?
faq.answer: The notice asks for ID proof and prefers an Aadhaar Card. You also need your CV, a photograph, and original and photocopied certificates.
